text:
Jack Quinn has waited a while for this. The eighth overall pick of 2020 is 25, and for the first time he is playing like a top-six winger in the minutes too: 19:14 a night, up from 15:39, and on the ice for 86 percent of Buffalo's power-play chances (37 percent last season). He has nine goals and 16 points in 16 games, and he opened the scoring against Columbus on November 6 by backhanding in his own rebound.

The finishing is running hot. He is shooting 20 percent against 10 last season, so expect fewer goals per shot. But his own chances are up too, to 1.20 expected goals per 60 from 0.96, and Buffalo carries 53.5 percent of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, more than without him. That is the part that makes this feel durable.

It is a turnaround from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level, mostly because opponents got so much with him on the ice (bottom 2 percent of forwards). Our projection lands around 33 goals. Watch his defensive numbers; they decide whether he keeps the minutes.
headline: Quinn finally has the minutes to match the talent
